rows.abstract: Rationale: It is a common expensive of an official or employee who is separated from the service through no fault of his own to find utter disapointment because he is not entitled to a separation benefit for lack of legal justification. This bill seeks to remedy this situation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 1998-11-19

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING JANUARY 1 OF EVERY YEAR AS "NATIONAL PULONG NG MGA BARANGAY DAY"
rows.abstract: Rationale: The proposed assemblage shall aim to instill in every citizen the importance of active participation in the governing machinery of the State. The Convention shall be the venue where concerned citizens can openly bring up issues like abuse, graft and corruption, etc. of government officials and employees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1998-11-19

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING PRIVATE INDUSTRIAL ENTERPRISES TO ISSUE REGULAR APPOINTMENTS TO PHYSICIANS EMPLOYED THEREIN AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREOF
rows.abstract: Employees of private industrial firms are request  to issue REGULAR APPOINTMENTS to physicians employed therein. The physicians shall thereafter be considered as regular employees. Penalizes violation of this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 1998-11-19

rows.author: A087
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING YEAR 2000 COMPLIANCE OF COMPUTER BASED PRODUCTS, PROVIDING INCENTIVES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES (y2k)
rows.abstract: "Year 2000 COMPLIANCE ACT OF 1998". This bill seeks to (1) promote free disclosure and exchange of information related to year 2000 readiness; (2) assist consumers, small business and local governments in effectivity and rapidly responding to year 2000 problems.
rows.status: Substituted by HB07083

rows.author: C012
rows.title_full: AN ACT ADJUSTING THE RATE OF SUBSIDIARY IMPRISONMENT FROM ONE DAY FOR EACH EIGHT PESOS (P8.00) TO ONE DAY FOR AN AMOUNT EQUIVALENT TO THE MINIMUM WAGE OF A LABORER IN THE NATIONAL CAPITAL REGION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 39 OF ACT NO. 3815,OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 5465
rows.abstract: Rationale: The reason for the adjustment is necessitated by the fact that the current  rate of "one day for each P8.00" subsidiary imprisonment is no longer realistic vis-a-vis the prevailing minimum wage rate.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1998-11-19

rows.author: C012
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE IMMEDIATE RELEASE OF AN ACCUSED WHO HAS UNDERGONE PREVENTIVE IMPRISONMENT FOR A PERIOD EQUAL TO OR MORE THAN THE MINIMUM IMPRISONMENT FOR THE OFFENSE CHARGE TO WHICH HE MAY BE SENTENCED, FURTHER AMENDING PARAGRAPH 3, ARTICLE 29OF ACT NO. 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 214
rows.abstract: This bill addresses the problem of jail congestion which has resulted in escapes, riots and disturbances, outbreaks of diseases among the inmates, as well as institutionaliz ation of jail gangs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1998-11-19

rows.author: C012
rows.title_full: AN ACT CONFERRING TO THE PROVINCIAL GOVERNOR, UPON THE RECOMMENDATION OF THE PROVINCIAL JAIL WARDEN, AND THE CHIEF, BUREAU OF JAIL MANAGEMENT AND PENOLOGY (BJMP) THE POWER TO GRANT ALLOWANCES FOR GOOD CONDUCT OF PRISONERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 99 OF ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: The author explains that prisoners wherenever they may be confined, must all be rewarded by law.  This bill also seeks to help decongest  on overly congested jails.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 280 OF THE LABOR CODE BY LIMITING THE NUMBER OF CASUAL AND CONTRACTUAL EMPLOYEES TO NOT MORE THAN TEN PERCENT (10%) OF THE EXISTING PERMANENT EMPLOYEES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Sixty percent (60%) of our labor force consists of casial and contractual employees who DO NOT enjoy the security of tenure and are earning incomes that could hardly answer for their daily needs.  The policy of multinational and transnational corporations in hiring a substantial percentage of these employees must be rectified.
